# Module `threads`

threads - pthread-backed threading and mutexes for Vyb.

A thread runs a `fn() -> Int` closure (no captures / no arguments in this
first cut — capturing closures are a later follow-on): thread_spawn starts it
and returns a handle, thread_join blocks until it finishes and returns the
closure's result. A Mutex provides mutual exclusion. Everything maps 1:1 onto
POSIX threads underneath, keeping the pthread ABI out of Vyb code.

Usage:
  import threads
  h = thread_spawn(|| -> 40 + 2)
  v = thread_join(h) else -2   // 42

  m = mutex_new() else 0
  mutex_lock(m); ... shared section ...; mutex_unlock(m)
  mutex_free(m)

  cv = cond_new() else 0                 // pair a condvar with a Mutex
  cond_wait(cv, m); cond_signal(cv); cond_broadcast(cv)

  cnt = atomic_new(0) else 0              // lock-free shared Int
  atomic_add(cnt, 1); atomic_load(cnt); atomic_cas(cnt, old, new)


<a id="sym-atomic_cas"></a>
### `atomic_cas` · fn

```
atomic_cas(a<Int>, expected<Int>, desired<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Atomically set the value to `desired` if it is currently `expected`; returns
a 1/0 probe -- 1 if the swap happened, else 0 (a value, not an op-status, so it
stays Int).

<a id="sym-thread_detach"></a>
### `thread_detach` · fn

```
thread_detach(handle<Int>)<Bool?> ->
```

Detach `handle`: the thread becomes non-joinable and its slot is reclaimed
automatically once its body returns (a reaper), so fire-and-forget workers
(e.g. per-connection HTTP handlers) can't exhaust the fixed thread table.
Returns `Bool?` -- present when detached, absent if the handle is
unknown/already-reaped or already detached.

<a id="sym-thread_join"></a>
### `thread_join` · fn

```
thread_join(handle<Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Wait for the thread `handle` to finish. Returns `Int?` -- present holding the
closure result (which may legitimately be any Int), absent when the handle is
unknown, detached, or already joined. A spawned thread's slot is only
reclaimed once it is joined. Unwrap with `else default` or `match`.

**Relationships**

- referenced by 1: [`https`](https.md)

<a id="sym-thread_spawn"></a>
### `thread_spawn` · fn

```
thread_spawn(work<fn() -> Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Start `work` on a new thread. Returns `Int?` -- present holding the thread
handle (>= 1) when the thread was created, absent when it could not be spawned
(thread-table full or pthread_create failed), so callers escalate the failure
with `else`/`match` instead of a `-1` sentinel. The handle-creators below
(mutex_new/cond_new/atomic_new) return `Int?`, and the mutex/cond/atomic
op-status helpers return `Bool?` (present on success). atomic_load,
atomic_add (returns the new value) and atomic_cas (1/0 probe) keep returning
their value/probe.

**Relationships**

- referenced by 2: [`http`](http.md), [`https`](https.md)
